comparisons.race: Texas Senate: how pollsters use the 2024 vote
comparisons.text:
How pollsters use the 2024 vote

Some polls adjust their sample using how people say they voted in 2024. These are the two groups’ average leads.

Uses 2024 vote
4.0 point lead
for James Talarico
1 poll · 1 pollster
Does not use it
1.2 point lead
for James Talarico
3 polls · 3 pollsters

Polls using 2024 votes read 2.8 points more favorably for James Talarico.

Different pollsters and dates may explain this gap. It does not establish which method is better.

Poll dates, sources and comparison details
+

“Uses 2024 vote” means reported past votes help determine how much weight respondents receive. “Does not use it” requires documented non-use. Unknown methods are left out.

These are different polls, not the same poll recalculated. Each pollster counts equally within its group; multiple polls from one firm are averaged first. These group readings use a different inclusion rule from the headline weighted average.

Compared: likely voters · full ballot. Dates are not matched.

Across this race, 7 polls have unverified recall weighting and are excluded from this comparison. Other voter groups and ballot formats are also excluded.

Uses 2024 vote
Siena Research Institute
↗
Oct 5–Oct 8 · Primary verified
Does not use it
Emerson College Polling
↗
Oct 17–Oct 19 · Primary verified
Marist Poll (Marist University)
↗
Oct 8–Oct 11 · Primary verified
Quantus Insights
↗
Oct 9–Oct 11 · Primary verified

Every comparison here is descriptive. None identifies the effect of recalled-vote weighting or its mechanism. Mode, timing, recruitment, screens, targets, nonresponse, pollster effects and selective publication remain confounded.
